"'''Shining Star'''" is a song by [[Earth, Wind & Fire]] from the album ''[[That's the Way of the World]]'', issued as a single in January 1975 on [[Columbia Records]].<ref name=Song>{{cite work|title=Earth, Wind & Fire: Shining Star|date=January 1975|publisher=Columbia Records}}</ref> The song rose to No. 1 on both the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart and the ''Billboard'' [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|Hot Soul Songs]] chart, becoming their first single to top both charts (and only single to top the former).<ref name=BBD>{{cite web|url= https://www.billboard.com/artist/earth-wind-fire/chart-history/hsi/|title=Earth, Wind & Fire: Shining Star (Hot 100)|website=billboard.com}}</ref><ref name=BB>{{cite web|url= https://www.billboard.com/artist/earth-wind-fire/chart-history/bsi/|title=Earth, Wind & Fire: Shining Star (Hot Soul Songs)|website=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref> It has also been certified [[RIAA certification|gold]] in the US by the [[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Gold & Platinum |url=https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&se=Earth%2C+Wind+%26+fire#search_section |website=RIAA |access-date=14 December 2020}}</ref>

"Shining Star" is a song by Earth, Wind & Fire from the album That's the Way of the World, issued as a single in January 1975 on Columbia Records. The song rose to No. 1 on both the Billboard Hot 100 chart and the Billboard Hot Soul Songs chart, becoming their first single to top both charts (and only single to top the former). It has also been certified gold in the US by the RIAA.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.wikitext:
"Shining Star" was produced by [[Maurice White]] and composed by White, [[Larry Dunn]] and [[Philip Bailey]]. 

The concept for the song came to Maurice White while strolling at night during the band's recording of ''[[That's the Way of the World]]'' at [[Caribou Ranch]]. He became inspired by looking up at the starry sky and took his ideas about the song to the other band members.<ref name=mixonline>{{cite web|url=http://mixonline.com/mag/audio_earth_wind_fires/|title=Classic Tracks: Earth, Wind & Fire's "Shining Star"|author=Flans, Robyn|date=December 1, 2004|publisher=Mixonline|website=mixonline.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091110222902/http://mixonline.com/mag/audio_earth_wind_fires/|archive-date=2009-11-10}}</ref>
sections.text:
"Shining Star" was produced by Maurice White and composed by White, Larry Dunn and Philip Bailey. 

The concept for the song came to Maurice White while strolling at night during the band's recording of That's the Way of the World at Caribou Ranch. He became inspired by looking up at the starry sky and took his ideas about the song to the other band members.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
''[[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]]'' called "Shining Star" a "treasure".<ref>{{cite magazine|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=yyYEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA205|title=Earth, Wind & Fire: That's The Way Of The World|page=205 |issue=9|volume=12|date=September 2004|magazine=[[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]]}}</ref> Alex Henderson of [[AllMusic]] described the song as "sweaty [[funk]]".<ref name="am">{{cite web|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/thats-the-way-of-the-world-mw0000650107|title=Earth, Wind & Fire: That's the Way of the World|author=Henderson, Alex|publisher=[[AllMusic]]}}</ref> Gordon Fletcher of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' wrote that the song "glow(s) with an incendiary charge that once moved record producer [[Sandy Pearlman]] to term EW&F 'the closest thing to a black [[Heavy metal music|heavy-metal]] band'."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/thats-the-way-of-the-world-205609/|title=Earth, Wind & Fire: That's The Way Of The World|first=Gordon|last=Fletcher |date=July 3, 1975|publisher=[[Rolling Stone]]|website=[[Rolling Stone]]}}</ref> Daryl Easlea of the [[BBC]] found that "'Shining Star' can be seen as much an influence on [[Prince (musician)|Prince]] as anything by [[James Brown]]".<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/music/reviews/wrb6 |title=Earth, Wind & Fire: That's the Way of the World Review|first=Daryl|last=Easlea|date=2010|publisher=[[BBC]]|website=bbc.co.uk}}</ref> Stephen Curwood of ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' noted that the tune "shows off the fabulous range and coordination of this nine-man vocal ensemble and instrumental choir.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/436578824/?terms=%22Earth%2C%2BWind%2B%26%2BFire%22&match=1|title=Records: Nelson, Earth etc., Bee Gees|page=11|date=July 18, 1975|author=Curwood, Stephen|publisher=[[Boston Globe]]|website=newspapers.com}}</ref>

"Shining Star" also won a [[Grammy Award for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals]] at the [[18th Annual Grammy Awards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.grammy.com/artists/earth-wind-fire/14550|title=Earth, Wind & Fire|publisher=[[The Recording Academy]]|website=grammy.com|date=23 November 2020}}</ref>
In 2008, the song was inducted into the [[Grammy Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{Cite web | title=GRAMMY Hall Of Fame {{!}} Hall of Fame Artists {{!}} GRAMMY.com | url=https://www.grammy.com/awards/hall-of-fame-award#s | access-date=2025-01-01 | website=www.grammy.com}}</ref>
sections.text:
Vibe called "Shining Star" a "treasure". Alex Henderson of AllMusic described the song as "sweaty funk". Gordon Fletcher of Rolling Stone wrote that the song "glow(s) with an incendiary charge that once moved record producer Sandy Pearlman to term EW&F 'the closest thing to a black heavy-metal band'." Daryl Easlea of the BBC found that "'Shining Star' can be seen as much an influence on Prince as anything by James Brown". Stephen Curwood of The Boston Globe noted that the tune "shows off the fabulous range and coordination of this nine-man vocal ensemble and instrumental choir.

"Shining Star" also won a Grammy Award for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals at the 18th Annual Grammy Awards.
In 2008, the song was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.

sections.heading: Covers and samples
sections.wikitext: The song has been sampled by hip hop artists [[MC Lyte]], [[Snoop Dogg]] and [[Salt-N-Pepa]] among many other artists. It has also been [[Interpolation (popular music)|interpolated]] in songs by [[hip-hop]] groups [[the Roots]] and [[De La Soul]].<ref>{{Citation |title=Earth, Wind & Fire – Shining Star |url=https://genius.com/Earth-wind-and-fire-shining-star-lyrics |access-date=2024-10-09 |publisher=Genius.com}}</ref>
sections.text: The song has been sampled by hip hop artists MC Lyte, Snoop Dogg and Salt-N-Pepa among many other artists. It has also been interpolated in songs by hip-hop groups the Roots and De La Soul.
